title: Control Plane Loop Registry
assertions: closed loops must bind business claims to code, tests, generated docs, and semantic hashes
business claim meaning changes must co-change at least one bound code or test file in pull requests
bound code or test file changes must co-change the claim registry manifest or generated claim evidence
harness loops must promote failures into closed-loop candidates by running tools/harnesspromotion and publishing strict candidate evidence
claim evidence must expose code, test, manifest, generated doc, verifier surface, and evidence chain ids so agents can infer required co-change and reasoning scope without reading prose
all loops with evidence expiry must declare a scheduled refresh workflow whose cadence is no slower than expiry and publishes strict evidence
loop registry and evidence graph evidence must carry generated_at and expires_at so tools can reject stale evidence
evidence graph evidence must expose full reasoning chains, not only chain ids
closed-loop candidate evidence artifacts must carry generated_at and expires_at so stale promotion, intake, and decision evidence can be rejected
refresh workflows must declare the loop ids they refresh so workflow edits cannot drift away from the loop registry manifest
provider acceptance harness loops must declare machine-readable provider coverage that matches provider QA observations
AI agents do not need to read the prose doc when the verifier can enforce the bound surface
loop evidence source kinds must use a machine-readable vocabulary so product QA evidence such as api snapshots and screenshots cannot drift into unverified free-form strings
loop registry evidence must expose loop surfaces so agents can derive QA scope without reopening the manifest or generated prose
loop registry evidence must expose a path-based architecture index so agents can select target verifiers without rereading the full manifest or generated prose
loop registry PR impact evidence must consume architecture_index and expose a target_verifier_plan for changed paths, architecture components, and focused claim commands

evidence_kinds.description: Structured machine-readable evidence emitted by a verifier or generator.
GitHub Actions artifact produced by a scheduled or PR workflow.
Reader-facing documentation generated from an executable SSOT manifest.
Redacted API request and response snapshot used as product or contract QA evidence.
Redacted UI screenshot or golden visual artifact used as product QA evidence.

harness_workflow_exclusions.reason: generated endpoint smoke matrix is a contract and generator gate, not a live exploratory harness that discovers runtime failures
harness promotion is the closed-loop candidate promotion sidecar consumed by harness loops, not a source harness

claim_bindings.statement: Deleting an agent must not delete or hide prior task thread replies, result messages, progress lines, or captured agent snapshot.

AI thread history must preserve user follow-up messages with their author identity, including execution-approval replies consumed by same-assignment pending tool approvals, and restore them after persistence reloads.
Multiple agents backed by the same provider must remain distinct assignments and threads across assignment, message posting, listing, and SSE filters.

AI thread history v3 must expose a stable conversation_id for agent comment card grouping, preserve that conversation_id for follow-up replies, expose parent_thread_id for follow-up runs, allocate a different conversation_id for same-agent reassignment, keep queued_by_busy_agent as a durable scheduler state but hide it from client-visible replies, v3 messages, v2 working thread projections, and queued work-status SSE events, suppress queued active streams after the same conversation has active running state, newer progress, or result history even when event timestamps arrive out of order, and omit active_stream when every v3 thread for the task is terminal so refresh can clear stale optimistic running UI.

AI thread history v3 must keep follow-up executions on a new assignment-scoped run identity, and render each thread timeline in deterministic user, progress-sequence, then agent-result order when timestamps tie.

Stopping an AI Agent task must target only the active assignment thread when assignment_id is omitted; it must not synthesize a stopped thread, mutate completed history, or make a just-stopped agent appear to keep working when the same agent is immediately reassigned.

Redacted live workflow summaries must declare generated_at and expires_at, and harness promotion must require generated_at < expires_at and now < expires_at before writing closed-loop candidate evidence.

Provider acceptance harness redacted summaries must expose verified codex_provider_qa, openclaw_provider_qa, and daemon_runtime_snapshot claims, and the harness loop must declare machine-readable codex/openclaw provider coverage matching those provider QA observations so the declared loop scope is visible without raw live output.

The AI Agent load and stress harness must run on a schedule, publish redacted live summary evidence, and promote failed runs into closed-loop candidate artifacts without exposing raw endpoint, token, or response data.

Control-plane high-traffic risk work must keep endpoint, store, SSE, subscriber fanout, assignment/tool-approval waiters, runtime progress, actor shutdown, local pressure, pprof, live load, architecture component surfaces, generated file architecture indexes, hot-path-to-file routing, executable target verifier commands, exact and directory-fallback file-level architecture query evidence, component role summaries, direct/fallback/miss query counts, and repo benchmark history records bound to lightweight benchmark evidence, local resource delta evidence, local CPU/heap/goroutine profile metadata, OTel/X-Ray/CloudWatch signal names, per-scenario capacity estimates, measured pressure findings, loopback-only profiling commands, redacted live-load commands, and explicit optimization candidates with closed-loop adoption paths and measured capacity/latency/allocation/cpu summaries without changing public API contracts.
Control-plane performance and high-traffic audit evidence artifacts must publish generated_at and expires_at so stale pressure and audit evidence cannot be reused as fresh loop input.

Sidecar-backed harness refresh workflows must run harnesspromotion and closed-loop candidate artifact upload under if: always(), every registered harness loop that runs harnesspromotion must have exactly one harness-promotion source with the same refresh workflow, and loop-owned candidate producer harnesses must be counted separately in harness-promotion evidence so a failing harness run still produces closed-loop candidate evidence without ambiguous source-count drift.

The generated endpoint smoke matrix workflow may be excluded from harness failure promotion only while it remains a contract and generator gate that proves OpenAPI generated-path parity, sorted matrix entries, v1/v2 generated endpoint smoke coverage, generated documentation freshness, and uploaded redacted evidence rather than a live exploratory harness.

Loop closure audit must compile the human-exit objective into executable checks that prove expired evidence refresh, claim-bound co-change, harness failure promotion, operational readiness partial promotion, provider coverage, pre-commit gating, evidence graph reasoning, compiled graph summary coverage, harness candidate artifact coverage, residual-gap candidate export, claim coverage token gaps, and claim coverage candidate export remain connected; claim coverage candidates must carry a structured subject with claim id, loop id, and missing coverage dimensions so follow-up work is machine-routable, and audit evidence must expose each check's verified proof status, proof count, proof key, concrete proof surface, claim-bound files, verifiers, generated docs, semantic hashes, loop surfaces, graph summary surfaces, harness summary surfaces, proof surface coverage, proof surface gap count, candidate artifact, promotion target, candidate count, and candidate ids.

Closed-loop candidate artifacts must include an adoption_plan that maps every required_next_artifact to an executable command, machine-routable candidate subjects may pin the intended next_artifact, intake evidence must expose candidate_adoption_plans, and intake/decision verifiers must reject candidates whose adoption plan is missing or incomplete.

Closed-loop candidate artifacts and harness promotion evidence must include promotion edges matching the source harness loop, closed-loop target, and promotes_failure_to relation, and a summary promotion run must expose promotion_result with candidate artifact, live status, candidate ids/count, and source freshness so agents can follow the failure-to-closed-loop path without reading narrative docs or opening the candidate artifact first.

Closed-loop candidate records must carry a source_ref that binds the source workflow, summary artifact, candidate artifact, source run, live status, and freshness window, and intake/decision evidence must expose candidate_source_refs while verifiers reject source_ref drift so copied candidate items keep their harness evidence context.

Closed-loop candidate records produced from harness failures must carry a machine-routable subject with kind, harness loop, source workflow, summary artifact, candidate artifact, live status, and claim id; intake, decision, and decision refresh command evidence must preserve the subject kind so follow-up agents can route failures without parsing observation or hypothesis text.
Closed-loop verifier tools must accept the common -verify intent as an alias for their generated-doc verification mode so agents do not need tool-specific flag memory.

Every redacted evidence artifact declared by an expiring loop must be produced by a scheduled refresh workflow that declares the loop id, fits the loop expiry window, and uploads that exact artifact with strict if-no-files-found behavior.

When task context is marketing, analysis, planning, or otherwise intent-oriented rather than an explicit instruction, the assignment prompt must emit intent_gate_required=true and require the agent to ask for intent in the existing thread before producing deliverables; provider token, quota, cloud-credit exhaustion, local approval-dialog wording, local command-permission wording, or runtime cancellation wording must render as a user-facing thread result without changing API shape; file/shell/tool permission must use the structured approval channel rather than conversational permission loops; an affirmative approval reply in the existing thread may approve only a same-assignment pending tool approval without creating a new assignment, and assigning another agent after the limit must create a separate conversation without hiding the prior thread history.

Loop registry evidence must expose each business claim's executable surface across code, tests, manifests, generated docs, verifier names, target verifier commands, and evidence graph chain ids, and each claim must bind at least one code or test path so agents can infer co-change, QA, and reasoning scope without reading narrative docs.

Loop registry evidence must expose each loop's observes, verifies, evidence sources, refresh workflow, expiry, fails_when, promotions, and provider coverage as loop_surfaces so agents can derive QA scope without reopening the manifest or generated prose.

Loop registry evidence must expose a generated architecture_index that maps bound paths and derived architecture components to claim ids, loop ids, verifier commands, and evidence chain ids, and generated docs must publish bounded component loop, claim, verifier, and evidence samples so agents can derive target verification from machine evidence without rereading the full manifest or generated prose.

Loop registry PR and local pre-commit impact evidence must consume architecture_index and expose a target_verifier_plan that maps changed paths and their derived architecture components to claim ids, loop ids, verifier commands, evidence chain ids, exact or component-routed match_kind, command_units that reverse-index each verifier command back to affected paths, components, loops, claims, and evidence chains, focused_commands that prioritize directly added, changed, removed, or bound-surface claim verifier commands, entrypoint_commands that rank the broadest verifier commands first, runnable_commands that precompute the exact command set a target verifier script will execute, path-level routing_packets plus routing packet/direct/fallback counts that prejoin each changed path to the runnable commands, claim ids, loop ids, evidence chain ids, direct command count, and fallback policy that apply to that path, and an optional executable target verifier shell script output that runs runnable_commands instead of asking agents to infer focused-versus-entrypoint policy; component-routed matches must cover new files inside known architecture components so agents do not infer verifier scope from prose or directory names; GitHub annotations plus local summaries must publish bounded target verifier path, component, loop, claim, evidence chain, focused command, entrypoint command, runnable command, route packet/direct/fallback counts, and command samples plus the full evidence artifact pointer so agents can start QA without reopening prose.

Loop registry coverage verification must centralize observes, verifies, fails_when, and evidence dimensions in an executable static registry, and loop-registry evidence plus generated docs must expose those dimensions so loop token extraction, claim token extraction, completion checks, and top-level verification dispatch co-change from one semantic table instead of duplicated per-dimension algorithms.

Every loop verifies token must be covered by at least one business claim in the same loop, and claim coverage tokens must reference declared loop verifies tokens, so QA scope is machine-derived instead of inferred from prose labels.

Every loop observes token must be covered by at least one business claim in the same loop, and claim coverage tokens must reference declared loop observes tokens, so observed failures and inputs are machine-derived instead of inferred from prose labels.

Every loop fails_when token must be covered by at least one business claim in the same loop, and claim failure coverage tokens must reference declared loop fails_when tokens, so failure semantics are machine-derived instead of inferred from prose labels.

Every loop evidence source path must be covered by at least one business claim in the same loop, and claim evidence coverage paths must reference declared loop evidence sources, so artifact-to-claim meaning is machine-derived instead of inferred from prose or artifact names.

Loop evidence source kinds must be declared in the Loop Registry evidence_kinds vocabulary, including json, workflow_artifact, generated_doc, api_snapshot, and screenshot, so QA modalities are machine-readable and unknown evidence kinds fail verification instead of becoming free-form prose.

Loop registry CI must emit GitHub Actions annotations for claim verifier commands, PR impact changed files, changed claim ids, changed claim generated evidence, reasoning evidence, claim-bound surface scope, and failed impact violation repair scope so reviewers and agents can see target QA commands, touched semantic surfaces, and required co-change repair directly in the check output without opening generated artifacts or narrative docs.

Evidence graph CI must emit GitHub Actions annotations for changed files, changed evidence chain ids, executable refs, claim ids, verifier commands, and next-loop targets so reviewers and agents can see observation-hypothesis-change-verifier-evidence-decision routing scope directly in the check output without opening generated artifacts or narrative docs.

When a business claim is added, its meaning changes, generated-doc binding changes, or a claim is removed in a pull request, the impact verifier must require at least one bound code or test path to change; manifest-only or generated-doc-only edits are not sufficient proof that runtime meaning was updated.

When a business claim meaning changes in a pull request, the impact verifier must require generated claim evidence and the evidence graph reasoning manifest to change so human-readable generated surfaces, Observation, Hypothesis, Decision, and Next Loop stay aligned with the changed claim.

When a claim-bound code or test path changes in a pull request, the impact verifier must require evidence graph reasoning movement in addition to generated-doc evidence so executable behavior changes keep human-readable generated surfaces, Observation, Hypothesis, Decision, and Next Loop aligned.

Loop registry impact evidence must expose the sorted changed_files list and failed co-change violations with claim id, scope, reason, required bound files, required generated evidence, required reasoning evidence, and observed changed surfaces, so agents and reviewers can infer PR impact scope and repair missing semantic co-change without rerunning git diff or reading narrative docs.

The local pre-commit hook and pull request workflow must run loop-registry generated-doc and impact verification with evidence output, target verifier summary, executable target verifier script output, and CI execution of that script, so claim-code-test-doc drift is blocked before PR creation and changed files route to runnable verifier commands before review.

The local pre-commit hook must run evidence-graph generated-doc and impact verification with evidence output, so observation, hypothesis, change, verifier, evidence, decision, and next-loop drift is blocked before PR creation.
Pre-commit baseline evidence must publish generated_at, expires_at, evidence_ttl_hours, and workflow_scheduled, and its workflow must run on a schedule with strict evidence artifact upload.

Workflow evidence must publish generated_at, expires_at, evidence_ttl_hours, workflow_scheduled, and strict_artifact_upload, and its workflow must run on a schedule with strict evidence artifact upload so workflow coverage cannot be reused after expiry.

Claim semantic hashes must ignore semantic_hash metadata values while still changing on statement, policy, verifier, bound file, or other semantic content changes, so refreshing evidence does not itself become a meaning change.
Every claim-bound code, test, fixture, manifest, and generated reader path must be covered by the loop-registry workflow trigger paths so PR impact verification runs when any bound surface changes.
Every loop-registry business claim must be referenced by at least one evidence-graph chain, and every chain claim reference must point to an existing loop-registry claim.
Every non-artifact file or workflow referenced by the evidence graph must be covered by the evidence-graph workflow trigger paths so graph verification runs when referenced surfaces move or change.

Evidence graph evidence must publish each chain's observation, hypothesis, changes, verifiers, evidence refs, decision, next loop, compiled chain summary, and next-loop summary so agents can infer why a loop exists and where it routes without opening narrative docs or recomputing graph-wide counts.

When an evidence graph chain is added, changed, or removed in a pull request, the evidence graph impact verifier must require at least one referenced executable change or verifier surface to move and expose the sorted changed_files list plus each impacted chain's claims, verifier refs, verifier commands, evidence refs, and next-loop target so reasoning-only edits cannot pass as closed-loop progress and follow-up agents do not need to rerun git diff or re-join the manifest.

Loop registry and evidence graph evidence artifacts must publish generated_at and expires_at, and the evidence graph workflow must run on a schedule no slower than its evidence TTL, upload the evidence artifact strictly, and expose a manual refresh command so stale reasoning graphs are refreshed without human reminders.

Harness promotion, closed-loop candidate intake, and closed-loop candidate decision evidence artifacts must publish generated_at and expires_at so stale candidate-loop evidence cannot be reused as fresh QA output.

Closed-loop candidate intake and decision consumers must parse source_generated_at and source_expires_at from candidate artifacts, require source_generated_at < source_expires_at and now < source_expires_at, and fail before producing intake or decision evidence so stale harness failures cannot become fresh closed-loop work.

Closed-loop candidate intake verification must consume a candidate artifact before producing intake evidence, preserve machine-routable candidate subjects with a kind when producers emit them, accept candidate-specific adoption artifacts only when they match subject next_artifact, and trigger when linked producer, loop registry, or evidence graph manifests change, so harness failures cannot become passive manifest-only reports.

Every loop with evidence expiry, regardless of expiry duration, must declare a scheduled refresh workflow whose cadence is no slower than the expiry and whose workflow publishes strict redacted evidence.

Every refresh workflow named by the loop registry must declare RIIDO_LOOP_IDS with the loop ids it refreshes, so workflow-only edits still expose their semantic loop ownership to verifiers and agents.

Loop registry evidence must expose a refresh_plan_summary plus per-loop refresh_plans that bind each expiring loop to its refresh workflow, cadence, expiry, next refresh due timestamp, evidence expiry timestamp, claim ids, verifier commands, ordered next commands, command-level claim ids and evidence chain ids, redacted evidence artifacts, and manual QA refresh command.

Loop registry must convert expired refresh_plans from existing evidence into ordered refresh command evidence, preserve command-level claim ids and evidence chain ids, publish that evidence as a strict loop-refresh-commands artifact, and include generated_at/expires_at freshness so scheduled automation can run expired QA without a human composing commands or trusting timeless command queues.

Loop refresh automation must consume only command evidence sources whose generated_at/expires_at windows are sane and currently valid after the command-producing workflows have run, merge repeated command inputs by intersecting their freshness windows, verify each source status and command_count against its payload, avoid shell-evaluating command strings, derive a validated workflow dispatch plan with a canonical verified_command plus structured safe workflow inputs, expose workflow dispatches with unioned loop_ids, claim_ids, and evidence_chain_ids, publish that workflow scope into GitHub Actions summary and notice output before dispatch, execute dispatches from structured workflow_file and input fields instead of evaling command strings, expose ignored non-workflow commands with loop_id, kind, command detail, upstream candidate subject identity, decision provenance, claim_ids, and evidence_chain_ids for follow-up agents, promote those ignored commands into a redacted closed-loop candidate artifact with machine-routable subject/source_ref/run/adoption_plan/verifier command binding that preserves claim/evidence-chain scope and decision provenance through a static command-to-subject binding registry, convert all-stale command evidence inputs into source_stale dispatch evidence plus redacted closed-loop candidates with stale-source subjects instead of missing artifacts, publish that plan and candidate artifact as strict generated_at/expires_at evidence linked to the merged source command evidence window or stale source list, keep the PR sample command source in a fixture shared by workflow and tests, write PR sample dispatch outputs under out/sample before copying them to final artifact names only on pull_request runs, clear final dispatch artifact paths before live non-PR generation so sample outputs cannot mask live download or dispatch generation failures, and dispatch only existing workflow basenames on non-PR runs.

Loop registry evidence must expose the executable evidence_graph edge list, not only edge counts, and every harness promotes_to target must have a matching promotes_failure_to graph edge so agents can infer loop-to-claim and harness-to-candidate paths from the artifact without opening narrative docs.

Every smoke, load, or harness workflow must either be registered as a harness loop that promotes failures into closed-loop candidates or be explicitly excluded with a machine-readable reason, replacement claim, and replacement evidence artifact that proves another executable surface owns the workflow.

Closed-loop candidate decision verification must consume a candidate artifact, preserve machine-routable candidate subjects with a kind when producers emit them, decision records or subject-kind decision templates must match that artifact except source_coverage_seed records, and its workflow must trigger when linked intake, producer, or loop registry manifests change: every candidate needs one decision, every non-seed decision must point to a current candidate unless a matching subject-kind template synthesizes the decision, and every intake source keeps a seed decision.

Closed-loop candidate decisions must choose a next_artifact that is explicitly required by the consumed candidate artifact, and when the candidate subject declares next_artifact the decision must select that machine-routable artifact so follow-up agents do not fall back to generic claim work.

Closed-loop candidate decision evidence must expose the owner, priority, disposition, review_by, decision_source, optional decision_template_subject_kind, executable next_command, and decision summary counts for registered decisions, consumed decisions, dispositions, priorities, next artifacts, and decision sources selected from the consumed candidate adoption_plan for the chosen next_artifact; generated docs must expose the stable registered decision summary, and the verifier must export selected commands as loop refresh command evidence while preserving source candidate id, subject kind, and decision provenance through a static refresh-command binding registry for copied, derived, and candidate-subject lookup fields.

Open decision queue questions must name an owner, bind a next executable artifact, expose a bounded next command, and keep the generated reader fresh so unresolved cross-repository boundaries stay executable instead of living in operator memory.

Operational release-prep checks must bind every monitoring, public QA status, usability, exception, stress, chaos, scenario, desktop, and Notion QA P0 backfill item to executable evidence; readiness evidence must carry its own expiry window, public status must expose only aggregate counts with raw logs and secrets excluded, that window must match the Loop Registry expiry, partial checks must expose their next artifact, placeholder-free executable command, at least one non-manual measurement signal, Notion QA cycles must bind page source, P0 priority, backfilled readiness check, next artifact, executable next command, and 24h workflow cadence, partial_promotion candidate ids/count as the first closed-loop candidate adoption step, and visual screenshot QA checks must use next commands that read issue body/comments while covered visual checks bind screenshot measurement evidence so agents do not infer unresolved readiness work from prose, server-only tests, a tracking issue, or unstructured Notion comments.

The public container image contract must bind Dockerfile parsing, required contract fields, build cache mounts, final image entrypoint, exposed port, non-root user, optional Fargate task IR checks, and module-decomposition ratchets to code, tests, and generated evidence so the runtime artifact shape cannot drift by prose or memory.

HTTP route handlers must remain split by client bootstrap, AI Agent assignment, thread-message, SSE stream, daemon agent, component-task, progress-ingest, and provider-status concepts, and top-level route registration must stay data-driven through a verified static route registry, so endpoint behavior is preserved while agents can inspect one route surface without loading the full server entrypoint.

loop.observation: AI agents can skip or misunderstand narrative docs, while previously fixed AI thread regressions can reappear when related files are edited independently.
loop.hypothesis: A loop registry can make the intended QA loop executable by binding business claims to code files, tests, generated docs, semantic hashes, evidence expiry, and harness promotion paths.
loop.execute: Generate this reader from the loop registry, verify claim-code-test-doc bindings, require each expiring loop to name a scheduled refresh workflow whose cadence is no slower than expiry and publishes strict evidence, require harness workflows to run tools/harnesspromotion and upload strict candidate evidence, compute claim semantic hashes, enforce PR impact co-change for claim meaning changes and bound file changes, and publish redacted evidence in CI.
loop.evaluate: The verifier fails on missing loop fields, missing tests, missing bound files, stale generated docs, missing scheduled refresh workflow coverage, refresh cadence slower than evidence expiry, missing strict refresh evidence, harness workflows without candidate promotion, unknown graph nodes, semantic hash drift, claim meaning changes without bound code/test changes, or bound code/test changes without claim evidence changes.
loop.retrospective: This moves the human out of the inner loop: a future AI can change code without reading this prose, but cannot merge drift without updating the executable claim binding and evidence.
